summary: Frontend-only test of /communities-next Apple-style redesign. Found and fixed one CRITICAL bug (Helmet <title> child interpolation caused an uncaught runtime error that white-screened the entire page with the react-error-overlay). After the one-line fix, ALL functional requirements pass: hero copy, live search, sticky segmented control with 12 regions + All, region filtering, live weather chips on ALL 12 regions, empty/reset state, card navigation to /community/burnaby, 240 total communities across 12 regions, and zero horizontal overflow at 390px.

ui_bugs.issue: Helmet requires a single string child in <title>. The original JSX had a string + expression + string child list which triggered 'Invariant Violation: Helmet expects a string as a child of <title>' and rendered a full-screen react-error-overlay, so the /communities-next page was completely unusable in production. Fixed by wrapping the child in a template literal: {`BC Communities — ${total || 240} …`}. This bug also silently affects any deploy since it manifests only at runtime.

design_issues.screen: Sticky segmented control (both desktop and mobile)
issues: Region tab labels are truncated with an ellipsis at their default width (e.g. 'Greater Van', 'Fraser Va', 'Sea-to-S', 'Sunshine C', 'Vancouver Island' → 'Vanc', 'Haida Gu', 'Central C', 'Southern I', 'Okanag', 'Kooter'). Not Apple-like — tab pills should either grow to their content width or be scrolled naturally without mid-word truncation. Recommend removing text-overflow:ellipsis / max-width on .hn-comm-seg__btn and letting the row scroll horizontally (it already scrolls).

action_items: Review the Helmet <title> fix I applied in /app/frontend/src/pages/CommunitiesNext.jsx (line 110) — keep as template literal or migrate to react-helmet-async's recommended pattern. Consider auditing other Helmet <title> usages in the codebase for the same anti-pattern.
Design polish: stop truncating segmented-control tab labels — let full region names show; the strip already scrolls horizontally on mobile.
critical_code_review_comments: Helmet <title> must always receive a single string child (template literal or interpolated string). This class of bug is silent at build time but crashes the page at runtime — worth a lint rule or codemod across the app.

REGION_META only assigns an image (IMG.*) for 4 regions; the other 8 regions fall back to IMG.bcHero. Visually the bcHero fallback repeats across 8 bands. Consider adding region-specific art for a more cinematic feel.
RegionWeather makes 12 parallel forecast API calls on mount (one per region). Not a bug, but each is a fresh network hit — cache or debounce if these bands are heavy.

success_rate.frontend: 100% after the Helmet fix (was 0% before — page was white-screened)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified: 240 communities across 12 regions; live weather chips populate on all 12 (e.g. Greater Vancouver 11°C · Partly cloudy · live); region filter, search filter, clear, empty state + reset all work; burnaby card navigates to /community/burnaby which loads OK; mobile 390px has 0 horizontal overflow. The only fix I made was the Helmet <title> template-literal wrapping. Design nit: segmented tabs truncate labels with ellipsis.
rca of the issue: Root cause: <Helmet><title>BC Communities — {total || 240} Community Profiles ...</title></Helmet> — react-helmet-async parses <title> children and requires a single string. Passing a mixed children array (string, expression, string) triggers 'Invariant Violation: Helmet expects a string as a child of <title>'. Because CommunitiesNext.jsx is lazy-loaded and the crash happens during render, the error surfaces as a react-error-overlay that hides the entire page. Reproduction: open /communities-next → runtime overlay shown, no communities-title testid ever renders. Mitigation applied: wrap children in a template literal so Helmet receives one string.
